note: On training goals he is a textbook good-to-great case and says so better than the ICP does — 'I'm already looking the way I want to look... I'm at the muscle mass I want to be at. So I would really just like to build up that cardiovascular endurance, that muscular endurance, and then that functional link between all my muscle groups.' At 5'4" and around 156 lb, training five days a week and walking daily, he is nowhere near the deconditioned exclusion. He misses the other three. He is a project manager at a managed services provider after 17 years in the Navy — a solid professional, but not the business owner or physician the stated criterion names, and his income position is the weakest in the batch: a credit score of 580-586, a new half-million-dollar mortgage, actively paying down debt, needing 12-month third-party financing at $650 a month and hunting for a Health Savings Account route to avoid touching household savings. And his health is not the neglected area, it is an unresolved medical crisis — a spine fracture with surgery anticipated, nerve blockers in the interim and a live medical board appeal. Recorded as outside because he fails three of five, but the classification is doing something misleading and the audit should say so: he is a highly motivated, well-informed prospect who has already used kettlebells under clinical supervision, and the only criterion that should genuinely give the business pause about him — whether a spine awaiting surgery should be under load at all — is the one the ICP still does not contain.
